title_en: Shanghai Jingang Economic and Trade General Corporation v. Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region Administration for Industry and Commerce — administrative penalty dispute
ruling_gist_en: According to the provisions of Articles 31 and 39 of the Administrative Penalty Law, before making an administrative penalty decision, the administrative organ shall inform the party of the facts, reasons, and basis for the decision, and also inform the party of the rights to which he is entitled; the written administrative penalty decision shall also contain the above necessary contents. If the administrative organ does not issue a formal written administrative penalty decision, but only issues a penalty certificate to the party without informing the party of the aforementioned necessary contents, making it impossible for the party to make a judgment, and the party directly files a lawsuit with the People's Court without administrative reconsideration, the People's Court shall accept it.

full_text_en:
Shanghai Jingang General Trade Company v.

Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region Administration for Industry and Commerce

— Administrative Penalty Case

[Ruling Summary]

Pursuant to the provisions of Articles 31 and 39 of the Administrative Penalty Law, before making an administrative penalty decision, an administrative organ shall inform the party of the facts, reasons, and basis for the decision, and shall also inform the party of the rights it enjoys according to law; the written decision on administrative penalty shall also contain the foregoing necessary contents. If the administrative organ fails to issue a formal written decision on administrative penalty, but merely issues a certificate of payment of the fine to the party, and fails to inform the party of the aforesaid necessary contents, thereby rendering the party unable to make a judgment, and the party therefore directly files a lawsuit with the People's Court without going through administrative reconsideration, the People's Court shall accept the case.

Supreme People's Court Administrative Ruling

(2005) Xing Ti Zi No. 1

Applicant for Retrial (plaintiff at first instance, appellant at second instance): Shanghai Jingang General Trade Company, domiciled at 3rd Floor, No. 920 Xiangyin Road, Shanghai.

Legal Representative: Zhang Yongming, General Manager.

Agent ad litem: Yi Tingbin, lawyer of Beijing Dongyuan Law Firm.

Respondent for Retrial (defendant at first instance, appellee at second instance): Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region Administration for Industry and Commerce, domiciled at No. 56 Renmin Road, Urumqi City, Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region.

Legal Representative: Tursun Abdureyim, Director of the Administration.

Agent ad litem: Shang Xiangyong, Assistant Inspector of the Administration.

Agent ad litem: Ding Xuan, Deputy Director of the Legal Affairs Division of the Administration.

Shanghai Jingang General Trade Company (hereinafter referred to as Jingang Company), in a dispute over administrative penalty filed against Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region Administration for Industry and Commerce (hereinafter referred to as Xinjiang AIC), refused to accept the administrative ruling (1998) Xin Xing Zhong Zi No. 9 of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region High People's Court, and filed an application for retrial with this Court. This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law, composed of Zhou Honggeng serving as Presiding Judge, and Acting Judges Meng Fanping and Wang Zhenyu, to hear this case. The trial has now been concluded.

On April 18, 1998, Jingang Company filed a lawsuit with the Urumqi Intermediate People's Court, alleging: In 1995, it arranged for the purchase and sale of off-plan cotton in Xinjiang for Jiangsu Province Zhangjiagang City Cotton and Jute Company, and was investigated and punished by Xinjiang AIC, fined RMB 1,000,000. On June 20, 1997, the Fair Trade Bureau of Xinjiang AIC issued a certificate stating: "Our Bureau received RMB 1,900,000 transferred by the Autonomous Region Cotton and Jute Company on February 17, 1996. Later, the Regional Cotton and Jute Company withdrew the temporarily deposited RMB 400,000 on April 2, 1996, and our Bureau actually received the penalty payment of RMB 1,500,000 (attached are two copies of relevant vouchers). Hereby certified." Xinjiang AIC illegally confiscated RMB 1,500,000 by means of a fine certificate. The company requested the court to annul the certificate, order Xinjiang AIC to return the RMB 1,500,000 cotton payment, and compensate for economic losses of RMB 200,000.

Xinjiang AIC argued in its defense: Pursuant to Article 11 of the Interim Regulations on Administrative Penalties for Speculative and Profiteering Activities and Article 38 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, Jingang Company, having failed to apply for administrative reconsideration or file an administrative lawsuit within the statutory time limit, had voluntarily abandoned its right to reconsideration and the right to appeal. It requested the court to dismiss the lawsuit.

The Urumqi Intermediate People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region held at first instance that the defendant, Xinjiang AIC, imposed the penalty on Jingang Company for its illegal cotton business activities in accordance with the Interim Regulations on Administrative Penalties for Speculative and Profiteering Activities. Pursuant to Article 11 of said Regulations, if the plaintiff, Jingang Company, refused to accept the administrative penalty, it should first apply for administrative reconsideration to the immediately higher-level administrative organ for industry and commerce; only if it still refused to accept the reconsideration decision could it file a lawsuit with the People's Court within the statutory time limit. The plaintiff's lawsuit did not satisfy the conditions for filing. The court ruled to dismiss the plaintiff's lawsuit.

Jingang Company refused to accept the ruling and appealed. The Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region High People's Court held at second instance that the grounds of appeal could not be sustained, and ruled to dismiss the appeal and uphold the original ruling.

Jingang Company, refusing to accept the second-instance ruling, applied to this Court for retrial, alleging: Xinjiang AIC directly seized RMB 1,500,000 of its funds without issuing a penalty decision, but merely issued a fine certificate afterwards by the Fair Trade Bureau of Xinjiang AIC. The certificate did not state the factual basis or legal basis for the penalty, nor did it inform of the right to appeal or the time limit for litigation. It requested the court to annul the original rulings, annul the fine certificate issued by Xinjiang AIC, return the RMB 1,500,000 cotton payment, and compensate for its economic losses of RMB 1,000,000.

Xinjiang AIC argued in its defense that Jingang Company had admitted its illegal conduct on June 17, 1997. Pursuant to Article 11 of the Interim Regulations on Administrative Penalties for Speculative and Profiteering Activities and Article 38 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, Jingang Company, having failed to apply for administrative reconsideration or file an administrative lawsuit within the statutory time limit, had its original ruling being reasonable, proper, and lawful, and requested its affirmance.

This Court holds: According to Articles 31 and 39 of the Administrative Penalty Law of the People's Republic of China, before making an administrative penalty decision, an administrative organ shall inform the party of the facts, reasons, and basis for the decision, and shall also inform the party of the rights it enjoys according to law; the written decision on administrative penalty shall also contain necessary contents such as "the facts and evidence of the party's violation of laws, regulations, or rules," "the type and basis of the administrative penalty," and "the channels and time limits for applying for administrative reconsideration or filing an administrative lawsuit if the party refuses to accept the administrative penalty decision." The fine certificate issued by Xinjiang AIC neither informed Jingang Company of the facts of its violation, nor informed it of the applicable legal basis. Under such circumstances, Jingang Company was unable to judge the nature of its conduct and the corresponding legal norms. The courts of first and second instance, on the ground that Jingang Company directly filed a lawsuit with the People's Court without going through administrative reconsideration, which did not comply with the provision on mandatory prior reconsideration under Article 11 of the Interim Regulations on Administrative Penalties for Speculative and Profiteering Activities, ruled to dismiss the case. Such ruling lacks legal basis. Pursuant to Article 22, Paragraph 1 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 79, Item (3) of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the ruling is as follows:

1. The administrative ruling (1998) Xin Xing Zhong Zi No. 9 of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region High People's Court is hereby vacated;

2. The administrative ruling (1998) Wu Zhong Xing Chu Zi No. 4 of the Urumqi Intermediate People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region is hereby vacated;

3. The Urumqi Intermediate People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region is hereby directed to conduct a trial of this case under the first-instance procedure.

Presiding Judge: Zhou Honggeng

Acting Judge: Meng Fanping

Acting Judge: Wang Zhenyu

November 3, 2005

Court Clerk: Zhao Hong

[Introduction of the Presiding Judge]

Senior Judge Zhou Honggeng: Born in 1948, holds a college degree in law. Served as a judge of the Supreme People's Court since 1993.
